reconstructed_theorem_text: For every natural number n with 3 ≤ n and every real number κ with 4 ≤ κ, let G = O(n, ℝ), let μ be the normalized Haar Borel probability measure on the full group G, and define νpos = 2 · (μ restricted to {O ∈ G : det O = 1}) and νneg = 2 · (μ restricted to {O ∈ G : det O = −1}). For O ∈ G, set Aκ(O) = ((κ + 1)/2) I − ((κ − 1)/4)(O + Oᵀ), and define γ(O) to be the centered multivariate Gaussian probability measure on ℝⁿ with covariance Aκ(O)⁻¹. Then γ is measurable as a map from G to the space of Borel measures on ℝⁿ, equipped with the sigma algebra generated by evaluation on Borel sets. The actual mixtures νpos.bind γ and νneg.bind γ, where ν.bind γ = join(map γ ν), are both probability measures. Moreover, for every Borel set B ⊆ ℝⁿ, (νpos.bind γ)(B) = ∫⁻_G γ(O)(B) dνpos(O), and for every Borel set B ⊆ ℝⁿ, (νneg.bind γ)(B) = ∫⁻_G γ(O)(B) dνneg(O).

The constructed mixtures are νpos.bind γ and νneg.bind γ, defined as join(map γ νpos) and join(map γ νneg).
